results.title: Modem Reboot Procedure
results.snippet: Reboot the modem when the customer reports: - No internet connection despite modem appearing powered on - Very slow speeds that did not improve after router restart

results.title: Slow Internet Speeds Troubleshooting
results.snippet: 1. **Weak modem signal** — downstream signal below -7 dBmV or above +7 dBmV indicates line issues. 2. **WiFi interference or distance** — 2.4 GHz band congestion; customer too far from router. 3. **Peak-hour congestion** — shared neighbourhood node oversubscribed in the evenings (6–10 PM).

results.title: WiFi vs. Ethernet — Troubleshooting Connectivity Differences
results.snippet: | Factor | Ethernet (wired) | WiFi (wireless) | |---|---|---| | Speed | Full subscribed tier | Up to 80% of tier (varies by band) |

data.text:
<analysis>
I've gathered the following diagnostic evidence:

**Account & Equipment** [tool:lookup_customer]:
- Jane Smith, active account since 2021, Gigabit 500 service tier in northeast (ZIP 10001)
- Equipment: NETGEAR CM500 modem, TP-Link Archer AX21 router

**Modem Status** [tool:check_modem_status]:
- Modem is online but showing critical issues:
  - Downstream signal: -12 dBmV (outside acceptable range; KB indicates -7 dBmV is the threshold)
  - Upstream signal: 44 dBmV (acceptable)
  - **7 restarts in the last 24 hours** — indicates line instability
  - Uptime only 0.5 hours (modem just restarted)
  - Signal quality rated as "weak"

**Connectivity Test** [tool:ping_customer_modem]:
- High latency: 287 ms (very high for a local modem)
- 12.5% packet loss — significant degradation
- Status: degraded

**ISP Outage Check** [tool:check_isp_outage]:
- No active outages in the customer's area (ZIP 10001)

**KB Findings** [kb:slow_speeds]:
- Weak downstream signal (below -7 dBmV) indicates a line issue, not WiFi or congestion
- The frequent restarts combined with weak signal strongly suggest a **line-level problem** (signal degradation on the ISP's network or last-mile connection)

**Diagnostic Conclusion:**
This is NOT a WiFi issue, peak-hour congestion, or equipment failure. The modem's weak downstream signal (-12 dBmV) and 7 restarts in 24 hours point to a **line quality issue** that requires ISP investigation. The customer needs to report this to the ISP for a technician visit to check the line from the pole to the house.
</analysis>

This isn't something you can fix on your end, so we'll need to send a technician out to check the line from the street to your house. Can I schedule that for you?
</reply>
